title: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 3, LOCALIZED OR GENERALIZED INTERMEDIATE, WITH BP230 DEFICIENCY

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3, localized or generalized intermediate, with BP230 deficiency (EBS3) is caused by homozygous or other biallelic mutation in the DST gene (113810) on chromosome 6p12.1.

paragraphs.text: EBS3 is an autosomal recessive inherited skin fragility disorder caused by intraepidermal separation. It is caused by loss of the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen-1 (BPAG1-e, BP230), which is encoded by the DST gene. Affected individuals have trauma-induced blisters and erosions. In the skin, hemidesmosomal inner plaques are lost and BPAG1-e is absent on immunostaining.

paragraphs.text: Groves et al. (2010) reported a 38-year-old man who had had generalized, trauma-induced spontaneous blisters and erosions all his life, particularly around the ankles. From age 37 years he also had episodic numbness in his limbs. The authors suggested that these neurologic symptoms might also be due to the DST mutation, but noted that he had a concomitant diagnosis of CADASIL (cerebral arteriopathy, autosomal dominant, with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy).

paragraphs.text: In a 38-year-old man with an inherited skin fragility disorder, Groves et al. (2010) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation (Q1124X) in the DST gene. The mutation lies in the region that encodes the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform BPAG1-e (BP230). It caused loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques and complete absence of BPAG1-e immunostaining in the patient's skin. The authors defined this as a new subtype of autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex.

paragraphs.text: Ganani et al. (2021) found biallelic DST mutations in 5 patients with epidermolysis bullosa simplex from 3 families. Two of the variants had not been reported before: a 1-bp duplication (c.7097dupA), which results in a tyr2366-to-ter (Y2366X) substitution, and a 1-bp deletion (c.7429delC), which results in a frameshift and premature termination (Leu2477SerfsTer13).

paragraphs.text: In a 38-year-old man with EBS3, Groves et al. (2010) identified a homozygous gln1124-to-ter (Q1124X) mutation in the DST gene. The mutation lies in the region that encodes the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform BPAG1-e. The patient had lifelong generalized, trauma-induced blisters and erosions. His skin showed loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques and complete absence of BPAG1-e immunostaining, as well as reduced labeling for plectin, beta-4 integrin, and type XVII collagen.
